title: Quiz: Mining Rules from the Health Insurance Dataset

questions.text: The rule {vision_cover} → {dental_cover} has lift = 2.1. What does this mean in a business context?
options: Vision cover causes dental cover purchases
Policyholders with vision cover buy dental cover 2.1× more often than the average policyholder
21% of all policyholders have both vision and dental cover
questions.explanation: Lift = 2.1 means this co-occurrence is 2.1 times more frequent than if the items were independent. It does NOT imply causation — it is a correlation. A natural confound is plan tier: Gold/Platinum holders are more likely to buy all add-ons.

questions.text: In arules, what does the %pin% operator do?
options: Pins a rule to the top of the results
Matches items using partial item name strings
Computes the proportion of rules containing an item
questions.explanation: %pin% is the 'partial item name' match operator in arules. subset(rules, rhs %pin% 'dental') returns all rules where the right-hand side contains the string 'dental'.

questions.text: When converting a data frame to an arules transactions object, you should include numeric variables like age and income to get richer rules.
questions.explanation: The transactions class is a binary (presence/absence) structure. Numeric variables must be discretised (e.g. age < 40 = TRUE) before they can be included. Passing raw numerics would produce meaningless results or an error.

questions.text: You find the rule {dental_cover, mental_cover} → {vision_cover} with confidence = 0.90. A product manager says 90% of policyholders who buy dental and mental cover also buy vision cover. Is this interpretation correct?
options: No — confidence measures support divided by item frequency
Yes — confidence = P(vision | dental ∩ mental) = 0.90 in this transaction set
No — confidence only applies to single-item antecedents
Yes, and this also proves vision causes dental and mental purchases
questions.explanation: Yes, the interpretation is correct. Confidence = P(consequent | antecedent) in the observed transaction data. However, correlation ≠ causation; the high confidence is likely explained by plan tier as a common cause.

questions.text: Which arulesViz plot type is most useful for exploring many rules simultaneously (support vs confidence, coloured by lift)?
questions.explanation: The scatter plot (method = 'scatter') maps support on the x-axis, confidence on the y-axis, and uses colour to encode lift. It is the most compact overview of a large rule set and makes the support-confidence-lift trade-off visible at a glance.
